items.title: トランプ氏、カナダとの貿易摩擦「かなり近く」合意する可能性を示唆
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： トランプ米大統領は12日、カナダとの貿易摩擦の解決に楽観的な見方を示し、北米の貿易協定から離脱する可能性に否定的な姿勢を示した。

ダブリンでアイルランドのマーティン首相と会談した際、米国・メキシコ・カナダ協定（USMCA）を離脱する考えがあるかと記者団に問われ、メキシコとは「素晴らしい関係」にあり、カナダとも実際には良好な関係にあると述べた。

トランプ氏は「かなり近いうち」にカナダとの合意が実現する可能性があると述べたが、正式な協議が再開したかどうかについて詳細は明らかにしなかった。カナダが米国の農家に「400%の関税」を課すなどしていると指摘し、そうした措置を見直し、高率の関税を撤廃する必要があるとトランプ氏は主張した。

米国とカナダの対立は関税問題にとどまらず、自動車など主要産業が依存するサプライチェーンを脅かすまでに拡大した。8月の包括的な貿易協議が土壇場で決裂した後、トランプ氏は数十億ドル相当のカナダ製品に50%の関税を課した。カナダのカーニー首相はこれを受けて、9月8日に報復関税を発動し、多くの米国製鉄鋼製品への関税を25%から50%へ引き上げた。

ただ、カーニー氏は最近、米国の最新措置による影響は全体として「限定的」だとして、新たな報復措置を取る可能性が低い可能性を示唆した。トランプ氏の発言とカーニー氏のこうした姿勢から、両国が緊張を和らげ、対立の出口を探っているとの期待が高まっている。一方、関係悪化を受け、トランプ氏がUSMCA離脱をちらつかせるとの懸念も出ていた。

カナダとの貿易戦争は、11月の中間選挙を控えるトランプ氏にとっても重大なリスクとなっている。関税の応酬は、有権者が懸念する物価高をさらに悪化させる恐れがあり、上院選で特に注目されるミシガン州など、カナダと国境を接する州の共和党にも逆風となる可能性がある。

原題：Trump Sees Canada Deal ‘Fairly Soon,’ Downplays Leaving USMCA（抜粋）

items.raw_description: India's central bank rejects Tata Sons request to avoid public listing, sources say    Reuters

items.title: India's central bank rejects Tata Sons request to avoid public listing, sources say
items.author: Jayshree Pyasi
items.creator: Jayshree Pyasi
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India, the country's central bank and banking regulator, has rejected an application from Tata Sons to deregister as a non-bank lender, two sources said, a decision that leaves the company closer to a stock market listing.
items.body:
The Reserve Bank of India, the country's central bank and banking regulator, has rejected an application from Tata Sons to deregister as a non-bank lender, two sources said, a decision that leaves the company closer to a stock market listing.
Tata Sons had applied to the RBI to deregister as a core investment company due to regulations that potentially require it to list.
The more than a century-old holding company, which controls businesses including Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS) , Tata Motors (TAMO.NS) , Tata Steel (TISC.NS) and Air India, has sought to remain privately held.
It is classified as a core investment company and falls under RBI regulations for non-bank lenders, which require that companies with assets exceeding 1 trillion rupees ($10.45 billion), or those with direct or indirect access to public funds, must list.
As of March 2025, Tata Sons' standalone assets totalled 1.75 trillion rupees.
The decision was communicated by the RBI in a letter on Saturday, the sources said, declining to be identified as they are not authorised to speak to the media.
Emails sent to the RBI, Tata Sons and Tata Trusts - the largest shareholder in Tata Sons - were not answered.
Until now, Tata Sons has remained unlisted. But pressure to go public has mounted this year from stakeholders including the second-largest shareholder, Shapoorji Pallonji Group.
Last month, Tata Sons said its chairman, N. Chandrasekaran, would not seek reappointment, plunging the group into uncertainty.
Chandrasekaran cited a lack of backing from the board as the reason behind his decision, following months of tensions with Tata Trusts, the charity arm that owns 66% of Tata Sons, Reuters [USN:L4N4490AW TEXT:"reported"].

items.title: Xi insta a los BRICS a desempeñar un rol en favor de la paz en Oriente Medio
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El presidente chino, Xi Jinping, instó al bloque BRICS a actuar como mediador en el conflicto de Oriente Medio, en un discurso pronunciado el sábado ante la cumbre de los países miembros celebrada en Nueva Delhi.
items.body:
El presidente chino, Xi Jinping, instó al bloque BRICS a actuar como mediador en el conflicto de Oriente Medio, en un discurso pronunciado el sábado ante la cumbre de los países miembros celebrada en Nueva Delhi.
China colaborará con los demás miembros del BRICS en esa función, ya que la guerra "no beneficia a los intereses comunes de la comunidad internacional", informó la cadena estatal CCTV citando las palabras de Xi.
El BRICS, compuesto originalmente por Brasil, Rusia, India, China y Sudáfrica, y ampliado para incluir a Egipto, Etiopía, Indonesia, Irán y los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, se creó en 2009 para desafiar un orden mundial dominado por Estados Unidos y sus aliados occidentales.
Sus miembros representan más del 40% de la población mundial y casi una cuarta parte de la economía global.
El líder chino calificó al bloque de "grupo líder" del Sur Global y de modelo de autosuficiencia entre los países emergentes y en desarrollo que debería promover un desarrollo impulsado por la innovación.
Según la CCTV, afirmó que China asumirá la presidencia del BRICS el próximo año y acogerá la cumbre 19 del BRICS.
En una reunión con el primer ministro indio, Narendra Modi, al margen de la cumbre, Xi afirmó que China considera las relaciones con la India desde una "perspectiva estratégica y a largo plazo", informó la agencia estatal de noticias Xinhua.
China y la India pueden aprender de los puntos fuertes de cada una y lograr un desarrollo compartido, citó Xinhua a Xi.
La visita de Xi a Nueva Delhi, la primera que realiza a la India en siete años, debería impulsar el deshielo diplomático entre estos dos gigantes vecinos, aunque, según los analistas, por el momento hay pocos indicios de que sus relaciones comerciales vayan a mejorar.
China y la India libraron una breve guerra en 1962, lo que sentó las bases para una relación marcada por la desconfianza desde entonces, que se deterioró tras un enfrentamiento fronterizo en 2020 en el que murieron 20 soldados indios y cuatro chinos.
Aun así, las relaciones han mejorado en los últimos años, especialmente desde que Modi visitó China el año pasado y dado que ambos países se enfrentan a relaciones inestables con Estados Unidos.

items.title: Anthropic CEO urges AI companies to slow model development amid fears over misuse
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Dario Amodei's essay comes after Anthropic released a threat intelligence report detailing how several actors used its Claude AI models for activities ranging from weapons development and cyber operations to surveillance and fraud.
items.body:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on AI companies to moderate the rate at which they advance model capabilities amid mounting fears of misuse of artificial intelligence, outlining a three-step framework intended to pace development and create more time to manage its risks.
"We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain," Amodei said in an essay shared on X.
His essay comes after Anthropic [USN:L8N4530XI TEXT:"released"] a threat intelligence report on Thursday detailing how several actors had used its Claude AI models for activities ranging from weapons development and cyber operations to surveillance and fraud.
Alarm about the potential harm from AI grew this week when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, stating that the "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade."
Amodei clarified that he was not calling for halting model training or technical progress, but ensuring that companies take adequate time to align and safeguard their models, and for third-party evaluators to confirm these steps.
As part of his proposed three-step framework, Amodei said Anthropic would install permanent third-party reviewers inside frontier AI companies, with access to relevant tools and internal risk-assessment processes.
Reuters reported last week that a swarm of rogue OpenAI agents [USN:L6N44W08B TEXT:"hijacked"] a German website and transformed it into a bulletin board for other AI agents, with the ChatGPT maker's officials keeping the incident under wraps as executives grappled with the fallout from the July breach of the open-source repository [USN:L1N44N0YE TEXT:"Hugging Face"].
Many incidents where AI agents from developers such as Anthropic's rival OpenAI have hacked or attempted to access external systems have heightened concerns over the increasing capacity of AI models and developers' ability to contain them.
Amodei said AI companies should voluntarily work together to set standards as growing numbers of U.S. lawmakers are calling for new rules to govern AI systems.

items.title: Piastri still hoping to win races to set up 2027 title bid
items.author: Alan Baldwin
items.creator: Alan Baldwin
items.summary: Oscar Piastri led Formula One by a healthy margin this time last year but now, with his title dreams effectively over for another season, the Australian says he is doing all he can to give himself the best shot at a championship challenge in 2027.
items.body:
Oscar Piastri led Formula One by a healthy margin this time last year but now, with his title dreams effectively over for another season, the Australian says he is doing all he can to give himself the best shot at a championship challenge in 2027.
That means winning at least one race to help rescue a disappointing year after the highs of 2025 and, with leaders Mercedes disappearing over the horizon, helping champions McLaren beat Ferrari to second place in the constructors' standings.
The 25-year-old was 31 points clear of British teammate Lando Norris, the eventual champion, at the top after the September 7 Italian Grand Prix last year and had won seven of 16 races.
Piastri left Monza this year still without a win to his credit after 13 rounds and 151 points behind Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli but fifth in that race and feeling he had taken "a much better step in the right direction.
"Of course, I would love to win a race or two this year, or more if I can," he told Reuters at the Spanish Grand Prix.
"But for me, honestly, the biggest thing, the end goal is to try and win championships. And if I can't do that this year, then I want to make sure I'm as best prepared as I can for next year."
REASONABLE CHANCE OF BEATING FERRARI Piastri's best result in the first season of the sport's new engine and rules era has been second place behind Antonelli in Japan last March, while teammate Lando Norris has won twice.
The Australian started the season with two 'did not starts', including one at home in Melbourne.
"Never say never but it is going to be incredibly challenging for the championship," said the Australian with typical deadpan understatement.
"(We're) trying to do the best we can in the constructors' championship because, whilst I think beating Mercedes is going to be tricky, I think we do have a reasonable chance of trying to beat Ferrari. Just trying to win races if we can and learn as much as we can for next year."
Ferrari are currently second, 59 points ahead of McLaren. Mercedes are 122 further in front.
Piastri's 2025 season nose-dived from a point where he seemed destined to take the title to being overtaken by Norris and then Red Bull's Max Verstappen, ending up third overall.
His most recent win was the Dutch Grand Prix in August last year.
The Australian denied that the knock-on effects of that campaign, and the mental toll of coming to terms with the crown slipping through his hands in what might even have been the opportunity of a lifetime, had seeped over into 2026.
"It's all to do with technically driving the car. There's nothing to do with a hangover from last year ... it's very much a technical thing," he said.
"It's not like I'm slow, feeling sorry for myself or thinking about last year. It's just that a few of the weekends I've had to drive the car in a different way that just hasn't really worked for me.
"The biggest thing this year has been the cars are very different to drive, both from a power unit point of view but also the car itself is fundamentally very different and the tyres also. There's just been a lot of challenges around that and how you extract performance out of the car.
"You've got to drive it very differently and I would say it's not necessarily in the way that I would choose to drive a race car. So there's just been some struggles getting to grips with that."

items.title: Trump dice que le "encantaría" ver una Irlanda unida
items.author: Bo Erickson, Padraic Halpin, Conor Humphries
items.creator: Bo Erickson, Padraic Halpin, Conor Humphries
items.summary: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el sábado que le "encantaría" que Irlanda del Norte, gobernada por el Reino Unido, se unificara con Irlanda, unas declaraciones realizadas durante una visita a Dublín que provocaron una dura reacción por parte de los unionistas probritánicos de Irlanda del Norte.
items.body:
El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el sábado que le "encantaría" que Irlanda del Norte, gobernada por el Reino Unido, se unificara con Irlanda, unas declaraciones realizadas durante una visita a Dublín que provocaron una dura reacción por parte de los unionistas probritánicos de Irlanda del Norte.
Los comentarios de Trump se producen semanas después de que el nuevo primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham, dijo que un referéndum sobre la salida de Irlanda del Norte del Reino Unido estaba "fuera de discusión". Downing Street afirmó el sábado que la postura se mantiene sin cambios.
"Bueno, no quiero causar ningún problema, pero les diré que me encantaría verla unificada", dijo Trump a periodistas sentados junto al primer ministro irlandés, Micheal Martin, tras la reunión que mantuvieron ambos en Dublín. "Al final va a suceder... Creo que sería algo fantástico".
"ALGO GENIAL" "Ahora bien, el Reino Unido tendrá algo que decir al respecto... pero creo que sería algo estupendo", añadió.
Trump dijo más tarde que "no había una buena respuesta" a la pregunta sobre la unidad de Irlanda, pero reiteró que pensaba que sería "algo genial".
Según los términos del Acuerdo del Viernes Santo de 1998, solo el Gobierno británico puede decidir si se celebra un referéndum sobre la salida de Irlanda del Norte del Reino Unido. El acuerdo puso fin a tres décadas de violencia entre los nacionalistas irlandeses, que buscaban una Irlanda unida, y los unionistas, que querían que Irlanda del Norte siguiera formando parte del Reino Unido.
Aunque las encuestas muestran que una cómoda mayoría en Irlanda del Norte está a favor de permanecer en el Reino Unido, la diferencia se ha reducido ligeramente desde que la salida de Londres de la Unión Europea situó la unidad en un lugar más destacado de la agenda política.
El líder del mayor partido unionista de Irlanda del Norte, el Partido Unionista Democrático, rechazó la predicción de Trump, afirmando que la unificación conduciría a "la destrucción de nuestro país".
"El futuro constitucional de Irlanda del Norte lo decidirá el pueblo de Irlanda del Norte, no los comentarios que se hagan en Londres, Dublín o Washington", escribió en X Gavin Robinson, quien en el pasado había apoyado públicamente a Trump.
Los anteriores presidentes de Estados Unidos, incluidos aquellos con un fuerte origen irlandés como Joe Biden, se han cuidado mucho de mantenerse neutrales respecto a la unificación de Irlanda. El Gobierno de Estados Unidos desempeñó un papel clave en la negociación del acuerdo de paz de 1998.
"NOS HAN DESPLUMADO" Trump realiza un viaje de 48 horas mientras su Partido Republicano hace campaña para mantener la mayoría en ambas cámaras del Congreso de Estados Unidos. Está previsto que asista a un torneo de golf en uno de sus complejos turísticos más tarde el sábado.
Trump también se reunió con la presidenta irlandesa, Catherine Connolly, elegida jefa de Estado el año pasado. Cuando Trump visitó Irlanda por última vez como presidente en 2019, Connolly, una política sin pelos en la lengua con opiniones de extrema izquierda en materia de política exterior, se manifestó frente al aeropuerto de Shannon, en el oeste de Irlanda.
Está previsto que el sábado se celebren manifestaciones contra la guerra y contra Trump en Dublín y en el oeste de Irlanda, cerca del Trump International Golf Links de Doonbeg.
Martin centró sus comentarios en los estrechos vínculos económicos entre ambos países.
Las empresas de propiedad estadounidense, principalmente de los sectores tecnológico y farmacéutico, dan empleo a alrededor del 10% de los trabajadores en Irlanda, después de que sucesivos gobiernos hayan dado prioridad a sus puestos de trabajo y a los ingresos fiscales que generan a lo largo de décadas.
"Se llevaron todas nuestras empresas médicas, tenemos que recuperar al menos un par de ellas", afirmó Trump.
"Nos han desplumado, pero no pasa nada... Hay mucho margen para todos y nuestra relación con ustedes es fantástica".

items.title: Rangers, Diamondbacks square off again in thick of wild-card races
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Arizona Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo had some advice for stretch-run observers.
items.body:
Arizona Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo had some advice for stretch-run observers.
"Buckle up," he said. "It's going to be awesome."
The Diamondbacks and Texas Rangers, both hunting for postseason spots, will continue their quest in the second game of a three-game series in Phoenix on Saturday night.
The D-backs scored the final nine runs in a 9-1 win on Friday.
"I know the guys are looking forward to just go out and compete," Lovullo said of his group, which has won five of its past six games. "These meaningful games are going to be the highlight of our season.
"You couldn't ask for anything more, to be sitting in this situation. It's what we love about this game."
Arizona's Brandon Pfaadt (7-2, 3.53 ERA) is scheduled to oppose Texas' Kumar Rocker (5-11, 4.61) in a matchup of right-handers on Saturday.
The D-backs (79-69) are one-half game behind San Diego (79-68) in the race for the third and final National League wild-card spot, and both are closing on wild-card leaders Philadelphia and the Chicago Cubs (both 82-66).
The Rangers (72-76), who have lost three games in a row, are three games behind Houston (75-73) for the AL West lead and three behind Cleveland (75-73) for the third AL wild-card spot.
Arizona right fielder Corbin Carroll homered Friday in his return to the lineup after missing two games with lower back discomfort. An MRI revealed no structural damage.
"Super positive news," Carroll said. "Just made me a little more confident to go out there and take these swings I need to take."
The Rangers appear close to adding a valuable piece of their own -- right-hander Nathan Eovaldi (10-9, 4.21 ERA) could be activated from the injured list Saturday. He could be used out of the bullpen, or as an occasional opener, since he has not pitched since Aug. 7.
"I love where he's at because he feels like he can help the team win right now and doesn't want to waste any more of these rehab assignments or anything else," Texas manager Skip Schumaker told The Dallas Morning News.
"He's a whole different arm, and that's the exciting part. I think it could provide a potential spark."
Pfaadt has sparked the D-backs since his return from the minors on June 30. He is 7-1 with a 2.38 ERA in 13 starts since beating San Francisco that day, and the D-backs are 11-2 in those outings.
Pfaadt gave up three runs in 6 1/3 innings his last time out at Houston on Saturday, when the D-backs rallied for a 4-3 victory in 10 innings.
He is 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA in three career appearances (two starts) against the Rangers. Pfaadt threw three scoreless innings of relief against them on May 12 in a game Arizona lost 7-4. Elias Diaz is 4-for-8 against Pfaadt, and Brandon Nimmo is 3-for-7.
Rocker's last outing Friday was in bulk relief as the Rangers sought to work around his 8.63 ERA in the first inning. He gave up six runs (five earned) and nine hits in five innings of a 7-6 loss to Tampa Bay, entering in the third inning.
"Whenever I'm called to take the ball in a big league game, that's what I do," said Rocker, who has followed an opener three times this season. "I try to go out there and compete to the fullest I can."
Rocker pitched five scoreless innings against the D-backs on May 13 but did not get a decision in the Rangers' 6-5 victory. Carroll is 0-for-1 with two walks against him.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Europe’s Solar Boom Has a Storage Problem
items.summary: Solar has become Europe’s largest source of power during summer months, helped by government incentives, falling technology costs and a rapid buildout across rooftops and utility-scale projects. But that success is creating a new problem: on sunny days, Europe can produce more solar power than the system can absorb, pushing wholesale electricity prices to zero or below and leaving some renewable generators suffering from their own success. Industry experts say the answer is not less solar, but more storage, more flexible demand and stronger grids that can move power from where it is generated to where it is needed. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: El cierre de un oleoducto saudí de vital importancia pone a Irak en una situación delicada
items.author: Devika Krishna Kumar, Khalid Al-Ansary
items.summary: El cierre del oleoducto Este-Oeste de Arabia Saudí provocó nuevas repercusiones el sábado, tras determinarse que los ataques se habían lanzado desde el interior de Irak.
items.body: Bloomberg — (Bloomberg) — El cierre del oleoducto Este-Oeste de Arabia Saudí provocó nuevas repercusiones el sábado, tras determinarse que los ataques se habían lanzado desde el interior de Irak. A primera hora del sábado, el primer ministro iraquí, Ali Al-Zaidi, destituyó al comandante de operaciones de la provincia de Maysan y ordenó una investigación tras constatar que los ataques contra el oleoducto procedían de un lugar situado dentro de la región, fronteriza con Irán, según un comunicado. VER MÁS: Arabia Saudita cierra oleoducto clave que evita el estrecho de Ormuz tras varios ataques Arabia Saudí cerró el oleoducto como medida de precaución el viernes, después de que varios drones atacaran la principal tubería en las regiones de Riad y Medina, según el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores saudí. Irak ha estado sometido a presiones para que intente impedir que las milicias locales respaldadas por Irán ayuden a otros grupos aliados en toda la región, pero ha tenido escaso éxito y su territorio se ha convertido en una base clave para las represalias de Teherán en todo el Golfo. Los combates se han intensificado en todo Oriente Medio en los últimos días: los hutíes, con base en Yemen, han afirmado que atacaron instalaciones energéticas saudíes en Abha, Najran y Jazan, mientras que EE. UU. llevó a cabo ataques contra petroleros iraníes. El oleoducto Este-Oeste ha demostrado ser un salvavidas crucial para las exportaciones de petróleo de Arabia Saudita, especialmente tras las perturbaciones provocadas por la guerra con Irán. El conducto, con una capacidad de 7 millones de barriles al día, alcanzó rápidamente su capacidad máxima a principios de este año, después de que el tráfico de petroleros quedara prácticamente paralizado en el estrecho de Ormuz. El oleoducto transporta el petróleo desde el Golfo Pérsico hacia el Mar Rojo, donde puede cargarse en petroleros. Sin embargo, esa ruta se ha visto sometida a presión en las últimas semanas por los ataques de los hutíes, respaldados por Irán. Estos han ganado terreno al tiempo que continúan lanzando ataques con misiles y drones contra Arabia Saudí, lo que ha obligado a este país a paralizar varias instalaciones energéticas. Un mayor control por parte del grupo les otorgará más poder para interrumpir el transporte marítimo a través de otro punto estratégico para el suministro energético, lo que aumentará la presión sobre los precios del petróleo, que ya se han disparado. Desde los ataques con drones, Irak también ha ordenado el cierre del paso fronterizo de Shalamcheh con Irán como medida de precaución, según informó Reuters, citando fuentes de seguridad no identificadas. Los ataques del jueves son “una demostración bastante clara de que tanto Irán como sus aliados tienen tanto la capacidad como la voluntad de atacar la infraestructura energética regional, y de que dicha infraestructura es vulnerable a los ataques con misiles balísticos o drones”, afirmó Gregory Brew, analista geopolítico de Eurasia Group. Los precios del petróleo apenas variaron tras la declaración del ministerio, y los futuros del Brent cotizaban en torno a los US$105 por barril. El Brent se disparó el jueves, llegando casi a los US$110, ante las especulaciones sobre el impacto de los últimos actos de violencia en el suministro energético de la región. “La magnitud de la interrupción ya se ha descontado en los precios”, señaló Brew. Las exportaciones de petróleo del reino se desplomaron hasta situarse en apenas unos 3 millones de barriles al día en agosto, la cifra más baja registrada desde principios de 2017, debido a los ataques perpetrados por militantes hutíes contra buques en el mar Rojo. La amenaza de los hutíes se produce en un momento en que el flujo de petróleo a través del estrecho de Ormuz sigue viéndose restringido. Estados Unidos ha impuesto un bloqueo a las cargas procedentes de los puertos iraníes, mientras que Teherán sigue atacando a los buques que transitan por el estrecho. Según ejecutivos del sector y datos de la agencia de seguimiento de petroleros Vortexa, a través de esta vía navegable en disputa se transportan actualmente alrededor de un millón de barriles diarios de productos petrolíferos, lo que supone un descenso respecto al nivel anterior a la guerra, que rondaba los cuatro millones de barriles. Como consecuencia, no solo están subiendo los precios del petróleo. Los precios mundiales de los combustibles también se han disparado. El precio medio al por menor de la gasolina en EE. UU. se sitúa por encima de los US$4 el galón, un máximo estacional, mientras que los precios medios al por menor del gasoil en EE. UU. se han disparado hasta alcanzar un récord de US$6 el galón. Varias reservas que ayudaron a amortiguar el suministro energético en los primeros días de la guerra se están agotando. Las reservas de petróleo de EE. UU. se han desplomado, mientras que la mayor parte de las reservas de emergencia liberadas por los gobiernos ya han llegado al mercado. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: No signed Hormuz deal expected yet from Oman meeting on Monday, Iranian official says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A meeting between Iran and Gulf states planned for Monday in Oman will be a chance to discuss issues including the Strait of Hormuz, but is not expected to yield a signed agreement over the blockaded waterway, a senior Iranian official said on Saturday.
items.body:
A meeting between Iran and Gulf states planned for Monday in Oman will be a chance to discuss issues including the Strait of Hormuz, but is not expected to yield a signed agreement over the blockaded waterway, a senior Iranian official said on Saturday.
Iran has been negotiating for months with Oman, which controls the opposite bank of the strait, over a deal that would govern transport through it. Oman has long said its negotiations are supported by other Arab countries in the Gulf.
Tehran announced on Friday that it was planning to attend a meeting with Gulf countries in Oman on Monday. Oman has not officially announced the meeting and other regional states have so far remained silent. Bahrain said on Saturday it would not attend meetings with Iran.
The Iranian official, who discussed the plans on condition of anonymity, said Monday's meeting was called at Oman's initiative, and would provide a forum to discuss other regional issues as well as Hormuz.
According to the Iranian official, Iran still wants an agreement that would allow it to collect fees from ships that use the strait, which Oman rejects.
Around a fifth of global oil supplies transited the strait before the United States and Israel attacked Iran in February, launching the war.
Global [USN:L1N45303L TEXT:"oil prices"] have surged over the past week after the United States and Iran both fired on tankers in the strait, and Iran's [USN:L6N4530LJ TEXT:"Houthi allies"] in Yemen advanced near another crucial Middle East conduit for oil, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula.

items.title: Ruthless Marquez beats Bezzecchi to win San Marino sprint, cuts Martin's lead
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Ducati's Marc Marquez pulled off the perfect getaway to beat Aprilia's home favourite Marco Bezzecchi and win Saturday's San Marino Grand Prix sprint, closing to within 14 points of MotoGP championship leader Jorge Martin who finished third.
items.body:
Ducati's Marc Marquez pulled off the perfect getaway to beat Aprilia's home favourite Marco Bezzecchi and win Saturday's San Marino Grand Prix sprint, closing to within 14 points of MotoGP championship leader Jorge Martin who finished third.
Bezzecchi had [USN:L4N454033 TEXT:"smashed the lap record to take pole"] ahead of Marquez in qualifying but it was the Ducati rider who had the perfect launch off the line before diving on the inside of turn one to storm into the lead.
From there, the reigning champion never looked back, though he had to work for his win as Bezzecchi initially matched his pace before Marquez found another gear to pull clear.
"Immediately when I started, the plan was to try to lead the race because I had the medium tyre and Bezzecchi was with the soft (tyre)," Marquez said.
"There were laps when they were a bit dangerous but then I tried to push. I see that I opened a gap. I tried to relax a bit and I saw that Marco was coming back.
"Then I attacked in the last laps because the pace was there. I was just trying to manage the risk. Happy with this victory, but the most important (race) is tomorrow."
Bezzecchi was initially faster in the early stages of the sprint but once Marquez got into his groove, he began setting fastest laps and built a lead of more than a second over the Aprilia rider by the halfway stage of the 13-lap sprint.
Fabio Di Giannantonio had slotted into third but his focus was more on Martin behind him as the Aprilia rider sought to limit any damage in the standings, with the Spaniard eventually moving up to third on lap seven with an overtake on the inside.
"Honestly, I didn't want to risk a lot to overtake him," Martin said. "I'm really happy with the job of the team ... and I hope that tomorrow we can improve a bit."
Bezzecchi managed to reel in Marquez to get within striking distance towards the end but the Ducati rider quickly responded with a race lap record on the penultimate lap before taking the chequered flag.
Bezzecchi, third in the standings, is now 22 points off top spot following his best sprint result of the season after finishing third four times.
"I'm very, very happy. My best result in the sprint - finally better than third, so it's a big result," he said.
Di Giannantonio finished fourth while Gresini Racing's Alex Marquez rounded out the top five. KTM's Pedro Acosta finished sixth followed by Raul Fernandez (Trackhouse), Fermin Aldeguer (Gresini) and Luca Marini (Honda) who finished in the points.

items.title: Hungary PM Magyar says to scrap Orban-era restriction on gay adoption
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Hungary's government will change legislation passed in 2020 by Viktor Orban's former government that had effectively banned gay adoption, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Saturday.
items.body:
Hungary's government will change legislation passed in 2020 by Viktor Orban's former government that had effectively banned gay adoption, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Saturday.
Adoption in Hungary, a European Union member state, by gay and lesbian couples was possible until late 2020 if one partner applied as a single person.
Under the law passed by Orban's right-wing Fidesz party in 2020, single people had to have their adoption requests approved by the family affairs minister, which has amounted to an effective ban.
Magyar ousted Orban after 16 years in a landslide election win in April. Changing the system of adoption would be a significant measure to restore LGBTQ rights.
"We can state unequivocally that we will change this system: it should not be the minister, a politician ... who makes the decision in such cases, but rather professionals capable of determining the conditions under which a given young child can achieve ... a life that allows them to become a happy and harmonious member of society," Magyar told a briefing, in reply to a question.
Orban, who cast himself as a defender of what he called Christian values from Western liberalism, [USN:L8N2ST395 TEXT:"passed laws"] ending the change of gender in personal documents, effectively halting adoption by same-sex couples and banning materials in schools seen as promoting homosexuality or gender transition.
The erosion of LGBTQ+ rights had a [USN:L8N3SK1J9 TEXT:"traumatic effect"] on the community.
Orban's government violated European law with rules prohibiting or restricting access to LGBTQ content, which stigmatise and marginalise gay and trans people, the European Court of Justice ruled in April, just before the election.
Hungary has never allowed gay marriage but still recognises civil unions.

items.title: With starting pitching in question, Phillies strive to even series vs. Braves
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Philadelphia dropped the opener of a three-game series against the host Atlanta Braves on Friday before Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly delivered even more bad news.
items.body:
Philadelphia dropped the opener of a three-game series against the host Atlanta Braves on Friday before Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly delivered even more bad news.
Left-hander Jesus Luzardo, who was scheduled to start Saturday night's game vs. the Braves, was scratched because of stiffness in his left shoulder.
"As we worked through it the last couple of days, we thought he's gonna be able to make the start," Mattingly said. "He's still not quite there. We feel like it's safer to be careful with him. We don't want this to linger, so it's one of those things, we want to try to take care of it and just go from there."
Mattingly said he hopes Luzardo (14-5, 2.87 ERA) will return to the mound next week.
"That's the first plan," Mattingly said. "Yeah, he needs just a couple extra days, works it out of there, and go from there."
The Phillies did not announce a starter for Saturday's game vs. the Braves, who will turn to right-hander Tyler Mahle (5-10, 4.05 ERA).
Philadelphia (82-66) trails National League East-leading Atlanta (87-61) by five games with 14 remaining after the Braves rallied in the 11th inning to win 6-5 in the series opener.
"You talk about a roller-coaster game, right?" Braves outfielder Brewer Hicklen said. "Up and down. Up and down, but you're just never out of it until the last out. It was really cool to be a part of, for sure."
Atlanta leads the season series 8-3.
Mahle has proved to be an important trade-deadline acquisition.
Although it wasn't the high-profile deal many expected, he consistently has performed at a high level and likely would be part of the team's postseason rotation.
Mahle pitched six innings in his last appearance against the Phillies on Sunday, allowing just two runs on four hits in his team's 5-4 victory. He retired the final 11 batters he faced and lowered his ERA to 1.24 in six starts since being acquired from San Francisco at the trade deadline. He has not allowed more than two runs since joining the Braves.
Mahle has made only three career starts against the Phillies, going 0-1 with a 2.70 ERA.
The Braves made a roster move on Friday, placing outfielder Lane Thomas on the 10-day injured list with a strained left intercostal muscle. The team recalled DaShawn Keirsey Jr. from Triple A Gwinnett; he was hitting .247 there, with six homers in 109 games.
The Braves and Phillies have become accustomed to high-profile games against each other. Since the current iteration of the NL East was formed in 1994, they have combined to win 25 of 31 total division titles. Philadelphia has won the last two, while the Braves won six straight from 2018-23.
"Any time you have two top teams in the same division going after each other, you know the history between these teams and you know the Braves' organization and the Phillies' organization have had really competitive teams," Atlanta pitcher Chris Sale said. "You feed off that energy and you realize when you're in it, you know what it is."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Kyle Leahy, Cardinals seek to prolong White Sox slump
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Amid a weekend celebration honoring their legendary stars and teams, the St. Louis Cardinals and their fans also can dream about the future of the club after promising performances by some of their best young players.
items.body:
Amid a weekend celebration honoring their legendary stars and teams, the St. Louis Cardinals and their fans also can dream about the future of the club after promising performances by some of their best young players.
On the other side of Busch Stadium, the visiting Chicago White Sox will try not to fret about handing over most of their lead in the American League Central with just over two weeks to go in the regular season.
The Cardinals will look to build on an encouraging victory in the series opener when they re-up with the White Sox (75-72) on Saturday night. After paying respect to the 2006 World Series club Friday night, the Cards beat the White Sox 7-3 behind strong hitting performances by rookies Joshua Baez and Leo Bernal.
The youngsters both went 3-for-4 with a pair of RBIs, and continue to produce quality major league at-bats. Baez, a 23-year-old outfielder, is slugging .580 with seven home runs in 88 at-bats. Bernal, a 22-year-old switch-hitting catcher, is slashing .325/.386/.525 in his first 10 big league games.
Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol added that Baez and Bernal, paired with the likes of Jordan Walker and Alec Burleson, make him optimistic about what the days and years ahead might bring. The Cardinals (73-75) are trying to avoid a third losing season out of the past four.
"At the moment and looking out into the future, there's a lot to be excited about with this young core," Marmol said. "Because, yes, the Burlys and Walkers are kind of understanding how to have consistent success, but Baez and Bernal -- you go down the list -- these guys are starting to get a taste of it. What they've been able to show to this point has been really good and promising. There's a lot to be optimistic about."
The White Sox had been teeming with optimism, surprisingly so, for most of the season after losing at least 100 games in each season from 2023-25. They had a 5 1/2 game lead in the division Aug. 16, and were ahead by 4 1/2 games as recently as two weeks ago.
But after dropping their fourth straight game Friday night, Chicago's lead on the Cleveland Guardians has disintegrated to just a half-game. The White Sox have scored a total of eight runs during their losing streak.
Left-hander Anthony Kay allowed three runs over four innings in dropping his fourth straight decision. Kay said he doesn't think the pressure of squandering a postseason cushion is getting to anyone.
"I don't think any of that is affecting us," Kay said. "Everyone knows what's ahead of us. We still have control over our own destiny, and we've got to keep chipping away each day.
"I think if you told us (before the season) that with 15 games left we'd have a division lead, I think everyone in this clubhouse would have signed up for it."
The White Sox and Guardians will go head-to-head for three games beginning Monday in Cleveland.
First, left-hander Sean Newcomb (2-4, 2.71 ERA) is slated to open for right-hander Luis Castillo on Saturday night. Castillo (4-11, 5.57) has a 7.52 ERA in six starts with Chicago since being acquired from the Seattle Mariners in a trade-deadline deal. Castillo has a 6-8 record and 4.34 ERA in 20 career starts against St. Louis.
The Cardinals counter with right-hander Kyle Leahy (10-4, 3.41). He is set to make his first career start against Chicago.
In addition to watching Baez, Bernal and other youngsters show what they can do, Marmol said he's looking forward to having them watch pregame ceremonies Saturday night, when St. Louis legends Albert Pujols and Yadier Molina will be inducted into the club's Hall of Fame.
"I want them to take that in and understand what it feels like to play here," Marmol said. "When you do it well, when you give everything you have to this organization, when you play the game the right way, and you're dedicated -- the way those guys were.
"Being young, being in that dugout, and witnessing that is pretty impactful."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Hamilton y Bearman chocan en última práctica del GP de España de la F1, Antonelli lidera
items.author: Alan Baldwin
items.creator: Alan Baldwin
items.summary: El piloto británico Lewis Hamilton estrelló el sábado su Ferrari en la última sesión de entrenamientos libres del Gran Premio de España en el nuevo circuito de Fórmula 1 de Madrid, lo que provocó la interrupción de la sesión a falta de poco más de media hora, mientras que el líder del campeonato de Mercedes, Kimi Antonelli, fue el más rápido.
items.body:
El piloto británico Lewis Hamilton estrelló el sábado su Ferrari en la última sesión de entrenamientos libres del Gran Premio de España en el nuevo circuito de Fórmula 1 de Madrid, lo que provocó la interrupción de la sesión a falta de poco más de media hora, mientras que el líder del campeonato de Mercedes, Kimi Antonelli, fue el más rápido.
El siete veces campeón del mundo, que ocupa un distante tercer lugar en la clasificación general, bloqueó los frenos y se estrelló contra las barreras en la última curva. Hamilton logró dar marcha atrás e intentó llevar el Ferrari dañado de vuelta al pit lane de Madring, prácticamente una vuelta completa, mientras ignoraba las instrucciones del equipo de detenerse.
Finalmente, el británico se detuvo, con el guardabarros delantero todavía encajado debajo del coche, que además tenía el neumático delantero derecho pinchado.
"Detén el coche. Detente en el lugar más seguro posible", le habían dicho antes.
"Si puedo regresar, lo haré. Si no, lo haré de forma segura", respondió Hamilton, quien regresó a los boxes en la parte trasera de una motocicleta después de estacionarse.
La sesión fue interrumpida y el cronómetro se detuvo temporalmente para reparar las barreras cuando faltaban 15 minutos para el final.
Tras la reanudación, Antonelli superó a Charles Leclerc de Ferrari, y se situó en lo más alto de la tabla de tiempos, con un minuto y 32,797 segundos, 0,166 segundos más rápido que el monegasco.
Tras 13 jornadas, Antonelli aventaja en 66 puntos a su compañero de equipo y rival más cercano, George Russell.
Bearman, de Haas, volvió a provocar la bandera roja en el último minuto cuando hizo un trompo y chocó contra las barreras con la cola en la curva 11, la aproximación a La Monumental, la curva peraltada más emblemática del circuito.
Oscar Piastri, de McLaren, fue el tercero más rápido, por delante del vigente campeón y compañero de equipo Lando Norris, con Max Verstappen de Red Bull quinto y Russell sexto.
Liam Lawson, de Red Bull, y Nico Hulkenberg, de Audi, fueron séptimo y octavo, respectivamente, mientras que Hamilton fue noveno y Gabriel Bortoleto, también de Audi, completó el top 10.
La sesión de clasificación se realizará más tarde y será crucial para la carrera del domingo, ya que es probable que los adelantamientos sean difíciles en un trazado exigente que, según dijo Russell el viernes, tiene menos margen de error que Mónaco debido a la proximidad de los muros, pero también a las mayores velocidades que se alcanzan.
"Nadie sabe realmente qué esperar. La sesión fue muy reñida. Se trata de completar una vuelta sin errores y sin tráfico", dijo el jefe de Mercedes, Toto Wolff.

items.title: El BRICS aprueba una declaración conjunta e insta a la "máxima moderación" en Oriente Medio
items.author: Sarita Singh
items.creator: Sarita Singh
items.summary: El grupo de países BRICS aprobó por unanimidad el sábado una declaración conjunta en la que expresaba su "profunda preocupación" por la guerra en Oriente Medio e instaba a la máxima moderación, abogando por un "enfoque multilateral" que respete los puntos de vista nacionales.
items.body:
El grupo de países BRICS aprobó por unanimidad el sábado una declaración conjunta en la que expresaba su "profunda preocupación" por la guerra en Oriente Medio e instaba a la máxima moderación, abogando por un "enfoque multilateral" que respete los puntos de vista nacionales.
La declaración, aprobada el primer día de la cumbre anual de líderes del BRICS en Nueva Delhi, se produce en un momento en el que Estados Unidos e Irán han reanudado los ataques recíprocos, tras una tregua en los combates durante gran parte del mes de agosto.
El bloque BRICS incluye tanto a Irán como a Emiratos Árabes Unidos, un aliado de Washington, lo que se esperaba que convirtiera en una tarea especialmente difícil para la anfitriona, Nueva Delhi, alcanzar un consenso sobre la declaración conjunta.
"Expresamos nuestra profunda preocupación por la continua escalada de tensiones en Oriente Medio... hacemos un llamamiento a que se actúe con la máxima moderación... y se eviten acciones que puedan agravar aún más la situación", reza la Declaración de Nueva Delhi.
La declaración también reiteró el compromiso de los países miembros con una resolución pacífica de las disputas internacionales "a través del diálogo, la consulta y la diplomacia".
Además, expresaron su preocupación por el aumento de las "medidas arancelarias y no arancelarias unilaterales" que distorsionan el comercio, en el contexto de las sanciones de Estados Unidos contra Teherán, en medio de su guerra con ese país, y contra Rusia por su conflicto con Ucrania.
El BRICS está formado por Brasil, Rusia, India, China, Sudáfrica, Egipto, Etiopía, Indonesia, Irán y los Emiratos Árabes Unidos.

items.summary: A lightning offensive by the Iran-aligned group puts the militants in a position to control a crucial Middle East waterway, creating a major new problem for Donald Trump as his war with Iran grinds on in its seventh month.
items.body:
A lightning offensive by the Iran-aligned Houthis has put the militants in a position to control a crucial Middle East waterway, creating a major new problem for U.S. President Donald Trump as his war with Iran grinds on in its seventh month.
Widening the Middle East conflict, Houthi fighters have advanced south along Yemen's coast, increasing their ability to choke off the Bab el-Mandeb Strait — the "Gate of Tears" at the mouth of the Red Sea — giving Tehran potential leverage over both of the region's main oil-shipping corridors.
The militants reached the island of Perim on Friday, in the middle of the strait between Yemen and Africa. That is bad news for Saudi Arabia, which has been shipping much of its oil from Red Sea ports since the war effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula.
It also comes at a difficult time for Trump, who is already grappling with record-low approval ratings and searching for a way out of the conflict, most recently by announcing an economic pressure campaign designed to force concessions from Iran's government.
High U.S. gasoline prices driven by the conflict have jeopardized his Republican Party's chances of keeping control of Congress in the November midterm elections. Iran remains defiant despite being hurt militarily and economically.
“Just weeks ago, Trump adopted a strategy of squeezing Iran's economy while keeping military conflict at levels too low to squeeze the American economy,” said Stephen Wertheim, a senior fellow at Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. “The Houthis have shattered Trump’s plan.”
DANGER OF JOINING THE FIGHT The U.S. administration can't afford to have the Houthis close the strait, driving up energy prices and disrupting global trade.
But at the same time, entering a fight with a foe that has [USN:L6N4500DZ TEXT:"withstood"] previous attacks by Saudi Arabia and the U.S. would be a dangerous new mission for a U.S. military already stretched by the fighting in Iran.
Saudi Arabia's de facto ruler, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, phoned Trump on Thursday and asked for U.S. military help fighting the Houthis, three sources told Reuters. He was told Washington would not intervene directly for now but would help with intelligence, the sources said.
Trump confirmed on Saturday that he had spoken to the crown prince, and said the Houthis had also phoned his administration and asked for Washington not to become directly involved in the conflict.
A senior Trump administration official declined to address specific questions, but said the U.S. is focused on national security interests such as ensuring freedom of navigation in the Red Sea "while empowering our regional partners to take the lead in managing and resolving regional security challenges”.
Saudi Arabia, Iran and the Houthis did not respond to a request for comment. Iran's foreign ministry said in a statement on Thursday that the Yemen conflict could not be solved by blockade or military action against the Houthis and called for dialogue, without addressing Iran's own role.
A SECOND KEY STRAIT Iran responded to U.S. and Israeli attacks earlier this year by disrupting the Strait of Hormuz, the outlet to the Gulf through which around a fifth of global oil supplies flowed before the war.
If the Houthis close the [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb"], that would deal another economic blow, constraining another 7% of global petroleum supplies and about 12% of global trade.
“This was always the worst-case scenario, that the Iranians exert control not only of Strait of Hormuz but Bab el-Mandeb, two of the leading energy choke points in the world,” said David Schenker, who served as Assistant Secretary of State for Near East Affairs during Trump’s first term and is now at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, a think tank.
"It's an enormous amount of leverage that [the Iranians] have in hand.”
Analysts and former officials say Trump now faces a choice: devote U.S. forces and scarce air-defense munitions to pushing back the Houthis, or leave Saudi Arabia and its allies, a Yemeni government based in the south, to confront them alone.
The Houthis seized Yemen's capital 12 years ago, and a Saudi-led military intervention has failed to dislodge them since.
Taking on the Houthis would effectively end a deal Trump struck last year in which the U.S. would stop bombing the group in exchange for a halt to strikes on Red Sea shipping. That would be likely to expose U.S. forces to missile attacks from Yemen.
A STRETCHED U.S. MILITARY It would also be another burden for the U.S. military.
U.S. officials say a fight with the Houthis could require significant naval and aerial [USN:L1N43N0P1 TEXT:"resources"] and divert U.S. intelligence assets, given the need to pinpoint Houthi positions that have changed since last year.
If U.S. Navy vessels and aircraft have to start shooting down Houthi drones and missiles, it could also worsen diminished stockpiles of U.S. munitions and air-defense interceptors.
The senior administration official denied that the U.S. was concerned about its resources being stretched. “The United States Military has more than enough munitions, ammo, and stockpiles to serve all of the Commander-in-Chief’s strategic goals and beyond,” the official said.
Tim Lenderking, who served as U.S. special envoy on Yemen under former President Joe Biden and is now a principal at law firm Squire Patton Boggs, said that with Trump signaling an unwillingness to get directly involved militarily against the Houthis, the U.S. needs to do more to share intelligence with the Saudis for their air campaign and step up diplomatic and material support for Yemen’s internationally recognized government.
“This administration came in asking the question, ‘What can Yemen do for us?’" Lenderking said during a webcast sponsored by the Middle East Institute think-tank in Washington. "Well, Yemen can spoil our day."

items.title: Playoff-bound Rays aim to take series from Astros
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays dramatically earned a playoff berth Friday night for the first time since 2023.
items.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays dramatically earned a playoff berth Friday night for the first time since 2023.
On Saturday, they will look to take the series from the Houston Astros in St. Petersburg, Fla.
The series opener could not have been scripted any better for the American League's top club, which is 88-59 and waited until the ninth inning to start readying playoff tickets.
Junior Caminero notched his first career walk-off hit with his AL-leading 40th blast to score pinch runner Jonny DeLuca, who ran for Jonathan Aranda after the first baseman nearly won it with a double off the top of the wall.
Caminero joined New York Yankees star Aaron Judge as the only players with current back-to-back 40-homer seasons.
"I was looking for a high pitch, and I was able to get it and send it out," said Caminero, who launched the Rays into the postseason for the sixth time in eight seasons in the 3-1 win.
Soaked in champagne, manager Kevin Cash said his team would savor the moment.
"We've been pretty consistent all season long," Cash said. "We thought this group was special. ... The guys are pumped in there and rightfully so. We've all acknowledged we want to continue this."
Starter Drew Rasmussen took a no-decision Friday after another sharp outing, allowing one run on eight hits in seven innings. The Rays are 10-0 since the All-Star break when Rasmussen takes the mound.
As the battle rages on against the in-state rival Texas Rangers, the AL West-leading Astros will turn to right-hander Peter Lambert (8-8, 3.67 ERA) and his seven-pitch repertoire to even the series.
In July, he was 2-0 with a 1.88 ERA in five starts with 32 strikeouts and eight walks in 28 2/3 innings.
According to Fangraphs, Lambert is one of a dozen pitchers to deliver seven different pitches 100 times or more.
He returned from his 2025 season in Japan with a robust arsenal of offerings - three fastballs, three breaking pitches and a changeup - and has excelled with the Astros (75-73) on the rotation's front end.
"I experimented with some different pitches (in Japan), but it never really stuck," said Lambert. "I was always a true four-pitch guy over there. With some help from the Astros, and it being a main focus of the offseason for me, I was able to get those pitches to stick."
Lambert is 1-0 with a 1.42 ERA in two starts and a relief appearance versus the Rays.
Slugger Yordan Alvarez (.310, 38 homers, 96 RBIs, 1.017 OPS) missed the opener with a sprained right ankle.
Tampa Bay's Ian Seymour will continue his chase for 10.
Since beating the Seattle Mariners on Aug. 9, the left-handed Seymour (9-6, 4.33) has been winless in five outings.
After moving to 9-3 by beating the M's with six innings of one-run ball, the 27-year-old Virginia Tech alum fell into a brutal stretch that saw him go 0-3 with a 5.19 ERA, though he did whiff 34 batters in his 26 innings pitched.
Firmly entrenched in one of the final two spots on the rotation's back end now but surely shifting to the bullpen in the playoffs, Seymour will be facing the Astros for the first time when he makes his 14th start and 44th appearance thus far.
-Field Level Media

items.title: With playoff berth secured after 20-0 rout, Brewers focus on rematch vs. Reds
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers acknowledged the importance of clinching their eighth postseason berth in nine seasons before quickly focusing on Saturday night's matchup with the visiting Cincinnati Reds.
items.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers acknowledged the importance of clinching their eighth postseason berth in nine seasons before quickly focusing on Saturday night's matchup with the visiting Cincinnati Reds.
The Brewers have not named a starting pitcher, although left-hander Kyle Harrison (10-4, 3.66 ERA) is a possibility after struggling mightily in his last two outings.
Right-hander Brady Singer (6-13, 5.03 ERA) will start on Saturday for the Reds.
The Brewers (92-56), bidding for their fourth consecutive National League Central title, clinched a playoff spot with a 20-0 rout of the Reds in the series opener Friday. Milwaukee, which is a franchise-record 36 games over .500, saw its magic number to clinch the division to four.
Garrett Mitchell had a grand slam, William Contreras homered and drove in a career-high six runs, and Dustin May threw six innings of two-hit ball in his best start since being acquired at the trade deadline from St. Louis last month. Brice Turang and Jake Bauers also went deep in the Brewers' 23-hit attack.
Milwaukee won its fourth consecutive contest to maintain its 10-game lead in the NL Central over the second-place Chicago Cubs (82-66), who defeated Pittsburgh 12-2. The Brewers remained 1 1/2 games ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers (90-57) in the race for the best overall record in the majors.
The Dodgers swept Milwaukee last season in the NL Championship Series.
"We'll have our hands full the next 14 games; that's just all there is to it," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. "I think it's important that we play a certain way and don't let our guard down. We're not going to do it at the risk of injury, but this isn't enough. This group in there, they want more."
Jackson Chourio continued his hot hitting with four hits Friday for Milwaukee. Chourio is batting .379 with six homers and 18 RBIs over his last 23 games.
Joey Ortiz also had four hits and is hitting .343 with two homers and nine RBIs in his last 21 games. Turang remained hot with three hits and four RBIs. He is batting .394 with 12 RBIs in his last 10 games.
Harrison has lasted just 3 2/3 innings in each of his last two outings, allowing a total of 15 runs (13 earned) on 19 hits. He was 8-1 with a 2.57 ERA at the end of June.
Harrison is 0-1 with a 6.27 ERA in four career appearances vs. Cincinnati.
The shutout loss on Friday was the largest in franchise history for the Reds, who used catcher Jose Trevino to pitch the final two innings.
"It's not a lot of fun to be a part of that," Cincinnati manager Terry Francona said afterward. "You try never to make a mockery of the game because people paid money to come, but you get to a point in the game where you don't want it to affect tomorrow."
Singer faced the Brewers his last time out, picking up the victory despite giving up six runs in five innings in a 12-8 win Sunday. He allowed four hits but walked a career-high six batters.
Singer is 1-3 with a 6.00 ERA in his last seven starts. His win over the Brewers last week was his first since July 22. He is 3-2 with a 4.70 ERA in six career starts against Milwaukee.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Saudíes cierran un oleoducto mientras hutíes refuerzan control sobre tráfico marítimo en el mar Rojo
items.author: Mohammed Ghobari, Eman Abouhassira, Yasmine Ghania
items.creator: Mohammed Ghobari, Eman Abouhassira, Yasmine Ghania
items.summary: Arabia Saudita cerró su oleoducto Este-Oeste después de que la vital vía de transporte de petróleo fue objeto de un ataque aéreo en el marco de una guerra en Oriente Medio en expansión, lo que amenaza con disparar aún más los precios de la energía.
items.body:
Arabia Saudita cerró su oleoducto Este-Oeste después de que la vital vía de transporte de petróleo fue objeto de un ataque aéreo en el marco de una guerra en Oriente Medio en expansión, lo que amenaza con disparar aún más los precios de la energía.
El mayor exportador mundial de crudo cerró temporalmente el oleoducto tras un ataque con drones que, según Bagdad y Riad, se originó en Irak, donde operan milicias respaldadas por Irán. Irak destituyó el sábado a un comandante militar en respuesta al ataque.
El oleoducto de 1.200 km (745 millas) que atraviesa la Península Arábiga había ayudado a Arabia Saudita a eludir el colapso del tráfico marítimo en el estrecho de Ormuz, donde el tráfico de petroleros se ha reducido a unos pocos al día debido a la guerra de seis meses entre Estados Unidos e Irán.
El Ministerio de Energía saudí dijo que había cerrado el oleoducto como medida de precaución. La línea ha transportado entre 4 y 5 millones de barriles al día en los últimos meses, lo que supone entre el 4% y el 5% del suministro mundial.
Nadie reivindicó de inmediato la autoría de los ataques. Las imágenes de satélite mostraban humo negro elevándose desde una zona del oleoducto al sur de Medina. El ataque provocó algunos heridos y daños que se estaban evaluando, informó el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores saudí, sin detallar el impacto en las exportaciones.
El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de visita en Irlanda para asistir a un torneo de golf en uno de sus complejos turísticos, dijo que probablemente Irán era el responsable del ataque.
Añadió que la guerra que él mismo inició hace seis meses probablemente terminaría poco después de las elecciones de mitad de mandato de noviembre en Estados Unidos, momento en el que los precios del petróleo "se desplomarían".
Los precios del petróleo se dispararon durante la semana pasada y el precio al por menor del diésel en Estados Unidos superó por primera vez la cifra récord de 6 dólares por galón, mientras tanto Estados Unidos como Irán atacaban petroleros en el Golfo y los hutíes de Yemen, alineados con Irán, reforzaban su control en el mar Rojo.
TRUMP CONFIRMA QUE HA HABLADO CON EL LÍDER SAUDÍ Cuatro fuentes del Gobierno yemení informaron a Reuters que los hutíes se habían apoderado el viernes de la estratégica isla de Perim, situada en la desembocadura del mar Rojo, en el estrecho de Bab el-Mandeb.
El gobernante de facto de Arabia Saudita, el príncipe heredero Mohammed bin Salman, llamó por teléfono a Trump la semana pasada y solicitó ayuda militar estadounidense para combatir a los hutíes, informaron dos fuentes a Reuters.
Se le comunicó que Washington no intervendría directamente por el momento, pero que prestaría ayuda en materia de inteligencia, añadieron las fuentes.
Trump confirmó el sábado que había hablado con el príncipe heredero y señaló que los hutíes también habían llamado a su Administración para pedir que Washington no se involucrara directamente en el conflicto.
Los dos ataques de los que se informó el viernes —contra el oleoducto y la isla de Perim— podrían suponer una peligrosa escalada, mientras que los esfuerzos diplomáticos para poner fin a la guerra se han estancado. El crudo saudí que se transporta a través del oleoducto hasta el mar Rojo ha sido la principal fuente alternativa de petróleo de Oriente Medio, dado que el acceso al Golfo ha estado cortado durante toda la guerra.
En una publicación en X el sábado, Ebrahim Azizi, presidente de la comisión de seguridad nacional del Parlamento iraní, dijo: "Mientras la parte estadounidense no acepte todas las condiciones de Irán, el diálogo y la negociación no sirven de nada".
Irán quiere que se reconozca su control sobre el estrecho de Ormuz, lo que le permitiría cobrar tasas a los buques que lo utilicen, algo que Washington rechaza. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores iraní afirmó el viernes que Irán se reuniría con los Estados del Golfo en Omán el lunes para debatir sobre el estrecho. Omán aún no ha confirmado públicamente dicha reunión.
El comandante militar iraquí destituido había dirigido operaciones en la provincia de Maysan, según el comunicado emitido el sábado por la oficina del primer ministro iraquí. La provincia, que limita con Irán en el sureste de Irak, se considera desde hace tiempo una zona en la que operan y mantienen su influencia las milicias chiíes respaldadas por Irán.
Arabia Saudita ha optado por no tomar represalias hasta el momento, a petición del primer ministro iraquí, indicó el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores saudí en un comunicado, aunque añadió que el reino se reserva el derecho a "tomar todas las medidas necesarias" para proteger sus intereses. El Gobierno iraquí ha condenado los ataques.
Irak ordenó el cierre del paso fronterizo de Shalamcheh con Irán como medida de precaución, informaron dos fuentes de seguridad a Reuters. Este paso fronterizo constituye una de las principales rutas para la importación a Irak de hortalizas y otros productos alimenticios procedentes de Irán.
Las dos fuentes indicaron que se estaba llevando a cabo una operación a gran escala para localizar a los responsables del ataque al oleoducto.
FUERZAS APOYADAS POR ARABIA SAUDITA PLANEAN UN CONTRATAQUE El suministro de crudo saudí cayó a los niveles más bajos en más de tres décadas, informó el viernes la Agencia Internacional de la Energía, en parte debido a los ataques contra buques que transitaban por Bab el-Mandeb perpetrados por grupos vinculados a los hutíes.
Las fuerzas del Gobierno yemení respaldadas por Arabia Saudita y con base en el sur indicaron que intentarían recuperar las zonas capturadas esta semana en la ofensiva relámpago de los hutíes, combatientes de montaña que tomaron la capital de Yemen hace 12 años y resistieron años de devastadores ataques aéreos saudíes durante la guerra civil yemení.
Reuters informó el jueves que el espectacular avance hutí a lo largo de la costa yemení del mar Rojo se produjo bajo la dirección directa de la Guardia Revolucionaria de Irán.
Irán ordenó a los hutíes la semana pasada que intensificaran sus ataques contra Arabia Saudita y les prometió más financiación, armas y oficiales de alto rango para ayudarles a hacerlo, afirmaron dos fuentes iraníes.
Irán describe a los hutíes como aliados, pero niega públicamente darles instrucciones militares.
El portavoz militar hutí, Yahya Saree, dijo que la navegación marítima seguía siendo segura para todos los buques, salvo para los saudíes, sujetos a una prohibición anunciada previamente.

items.title: Danish FA chief says FIFA Legal Committee evaded questions on Infantino proposal
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Denmark's football chief said on Saturday that FIFA declined to answer "critical questions" at a Legal Committee meeting about its abandoned proposal to sell commercial stakes in tournaments as he renewed calls for President Gianni Infantino to step down.
items.body:
Denmark's football chief said on Saturday that FIFA declined to answer "critical questions" at a Legal Committee meeting about its abandoned proposal to sell commercial stakes in tournaments as he renewed calls for President Gianni Infantino to step down.
Danish FA (DBU) President Jesper Moller said he was surprised that the [USN:L1N43X04P TEXT:"now-abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise"] was not on the agenda and was frustrated by the world soccer governing body's evasive response to his inquiries.
"I naturally used the meeting to ask a number of critical questions about the process, which I still consider to have been deeply problematic," Moller said in a statement.
"I am surprised that FIFA Forward Enterprise has not been discussed by the Legal Committee, which is precisely the body that should be consulted on legal matters concerning FIFA.
"But unfortunately, it proved impossible to get answers to the questions, as FIFA wants to await the discussion at the upcoming Council meeting in October.
"This would clearly have been a good opportunity for FIFA's leadership to explain itself."
Reuters has contacted FIFA for comment.
The FIFA Council comprises 37 members including president Infantino, eight vice-presidents and 28 other members elected by the member associations.
"We will continue to push for answers and I am confident that we will get to the bottom of this completely unacceptable matter," Moller added.
"The meeting confirmed that FIFA cannot rebuild its credibility under the current leadership. The time has come for a change of president at FIFA."
'CREDIBLE ALTERNATIVE' TO INFANTINO Last month, the [USN:L4N44I0QX TEXT:"DBU vowed to find a credible alternative"] to Infantino in next year's election, saying it had lost confidence in the Swiss-Italian after his aborted proposal to sell commercial stakes in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.
"I will continue working closely with my European colleagues to find a candidate who can command a majority. There is no trust in Infantino and FIFA's leadership," Moller said.
FIFA had apologised to member associations for mistakes made over the abandoned proposal, but its leadership reaffirmed support for Infantino after a crisis meeting in Morocco.
The DBU said Infantino's proposal had created "a fundamental crisis of confidence in FIFA's leadership" that could not be repaired by withdrawals or apologies.
However, [USN:L6N4520VY TEXT:"Infantino can count on enough votes"] to win re-election, meaning his opponents will need to shift strategy and focus on curbing his powers, multiple sources familiar with the discussions told Reuters.
The FIFA presidential election will take place in Rabat on March 18, 2027.
Infantino's plan prompted a global backlash, with UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and North America's CONCACAF among those calling for change at the top of FIFA while the possibility of a [USN:L6N44G0N5 TEXT:"no-confidence vote"] was also discussed.
Several European national associations have since withdrawn backing for Infantino's re-election, including the [USN:L6N4510X8 TEXT:"French Football Federation"] on Thursday, while Austria's FA (OFB) also withdrew support.
"The Supervisory Board of the OFB unanimously decided not to support Gianni Infantino's renewed candidacy as FIFA President," it said in a statement.
"The basis for this decision is the developments of recent weeks and months and the resulting significant changes in the framework conditions."

Danish FA (DBU) President Jesper Moller said he was surprised that the now-abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise was not on the agenda and was frustrated by the world soccer governing body's evasive response to his inquiries.
"I naturally used the meeting to ask a number of critical questions about the process, which I still consider to have been deeply problematic," Moller said in a statement.
"I am surprised that FIFA Forward Enterprise has not been discussed by the Legal Committee, which is precisely the body that should be consulted on legal matters concerning FIFA.

"But unfortunately, it proved impossible to get answers to the questions, as FIFA wants to await the discussion at the upcoming Council meeting in October.
"This would clearly have been a good opportunity for FIFA's leadership to explain itself."
Reuters has contacted FIFA for comment.
The FIFA Council comprises 37 members including president Infantino, eight vice-presidents and 28 other members elected by the member associations.
"We will continue to push for answers and I am confident that we will get to the bottom of this completely unacceptable matter," Moller added.
"The meeting confirmed that FIFA cannot rebuild its credibility under the current leadership. The time has come for a change of president at FIFA."
'CREDIBLE ALTERNATIVE' TO INFANTINO
Last month, the DBU vowed to find a credible alternative to Infantino in next year's election, saying it had lost confidence in the Swiss-Italian after his aborted proposal to sell commercial stakes in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.
"I will continue working closely with my European colleagues to find a candidate who can command a majority. There is no trust in Infantino and FIFA's leadership," Moller said.
FIFA had apologised to member associations for mistakes made over the abandoned proposal, but its leadership reaffirmed support for Infantino after a crisis meeting in Morocco.
The DBU said Infantino's proposal had created "a fundamental crisis of confidence in FIFA's leadership" that could not be repaired by withdrawals or apologies.
However, Infantino can count on enough votes to win re-election, meaning his opponents will need to shift strategy and focus on curbing his powers, multiple sources familiar with the discussions told Reuters.
The FIFA presidential election will take place in Rabat on March 18, 2027.
Infantino's plan prompted a global backlash, with UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and North America's CONCACAF among those calling for change at the top of FIFA while the possibility of a no-confidence vote was also discussed.
Several European national associations have since withdrawn backing for Infantino's re-election, including the French Football Federation on Thursday, while Austria's FA (OFB) also withdrew support.
"The Supervisory Board of the OFB unanimously decided not to support Gianni Infantino's renewed candidacy as FIFA President," it said in a statement.
"The basis for this decision is the developments of recent weeks and months and the resulting significant changes in the framework conditions."

items.title: GB-Reform UK a reçu deux dons de €42 mlns de crypto-milliardaires en 48 heures
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Reform UK a reçu un deuxième don de 36 millions de livres sterling (42 millions d'euros) en l'espace de 48 heures, a annoncé samedi son auteur, alors que le parti populiste anti-immigration de Nigel Farage vise la victoire aux élections législatives prévues d'ici à la mi-2029.
items.body:
Reform UK a reçu un deuxième don de 36 millions de livres sterling (42 millions d'euros) en l'espace de 48 heures, a annoncé samedi son auteur, alors que le parti populiste anti-immigration de Nigel Farage vise la victoire aux élections législatives prévues d'ici à la mi-2029.
Le milliardaire des cryptomonnaies Christopher Harborne, déjà le plus grand donateur de Reform UK, annonce dans les colonnes du journal The Telegraph qu'il a fait un don similaire à celui d'un autre crypto-milliardaire, Ben Delo, qui avait été condamné en 2022 aux États-Unis pour violation de la loi sur le secret bancaire avant d'être gracié par Donald Trump.
"Un pays fort est un pays qui s'appuie sur une économie dynamique, créatrice d'emplois. C'est pourquoi j'investis mon argent dans ce que je considère comme la seule cause viable capable de mener à bien la relance", écrit Christopher Harborne, qui a déjà donné près de 100 millions de livres à Reform UK.
"Je pense que Nigel Farage et son parti comprennent parfaitement ce qu'un gouvernement doit faire pour remettre notre pays sur la bonne voie.
"Alors que je versais chaque mois environ 1 million de livres sterling à Reform, Ben Delo m'a annoncé qu'il allait faire un don record de 36 millions de livres sterling. Mon esprit de compétition m'a poussé à égaler ce montant, et c'est ce que j'ai fait", ajoute l'investisseur.
Nigel Farage a promis de transformer son pays en "Hub crypto" s'il parvient au pouvoir.
Les donations individuelles aux partis politiques ne sont pas plafonnées au Royaume-uni, comme c'est le cas en France par exemple, à condition que le donateur soit domicilié sur le sol britannique, ce qui est le cas des deux milliardaires, Ben Delo ayant récemment rapatrié son domicile fiscal de Hong Kong à la Grande-Bretagne.
